title: ADA News: ADA calls for greater oversight of dental insurance markets (September 18, 2026)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: American Dental Association (ADA News, association publication)
source_type: Advocacy organization news article summarizing a letter to Congress
reliability: Advocacy organization's own news service describing its comments to a House subcommittee; reports positions, not independent measurements.
findings: The ADA urged Congress to include dental insurance markets in competition oversight and to avoid new broad burdens on independent dental practices.

According to the ADA's letter, manual verification of varying plan designs creates administrative burdens for dental practices; the ADA urged greater automation of dental administrative transactions in Medicare Advantage, including standardized electronic eligibility and benefit verification.
The article states the ADA wrote that insurers should not use AI as the sole basis for claim denials or prior authorization decisions.
limitations: Article summary only; the underlying letter was not read.
ADA position, not measured burden; no quantification of verification time or cost.
Concerns Medicare Advantage supplemental dental and policy advocacy, not small-practice cost data.
